title: Pikachu Plush Completes 67-Day Space Station Visit
summary:
The European Space Agency (ESA) revealed on September 19, 2026, that a special Pikachu plush had spent 67 days on the International Space Station (ISS). The toy went to the ISS on a Cygnus cargo spacecraft on April 11. It returned to Earth on June 17 aboard a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. During its time in orbit, Pikachu completed about 1,040 trips around Earth.

The mission was part of ESA's plans to celebrate World Space Week 2026, which will be held from October 4 through 10. To mark the occasion, ESA has created a special exhibit that combines real space science with Pokémon characters. It includes themed displays of Europe's space missions and life aboard the ISS. Visitors can also explore how ESA studies the Sun, the Solar System, and the wider universe.

The exhibit tour began at ESA headquarters in Paris, France, in late September. It will then travel to museums and other venues across Europe through April 2027.

Fans of the Pokémon GO game will also be able to join the space-themed activities. From October 4, 2026, through April 30, 2027, players visiting participating science and space museums across Europe can take part. Activities include One-Star Raids featuring Astronaut Pikachu and research tasks. There will also be chances to encounter event-themed Pokémon.

ESA hopes the project will spark curiosity about space and science in children and teens. "Inspiring future generations is a key part of ESA's mission," said Josef Aschbacher, the Director General of ESA.
why_it_matters: ESA's project gives museum visitors a way to explore space science through Pokémon-themed displays and activities. Its stated goal is to spark scientific curiosity in children and teens.
